meta.title: What does a story lose each time it's retold? | The Part That Doesn't Fit
meta.description:
An indie folk-pop song about a family story worn smooth by retelling, and an AI voice that promises to keep the part that doesn't fit. Two voices, one old wedding tale, a chorus to sing back.

For a Mercury retrograde, when astrology reads a call to slow down and reread: this song goes back over a story to keep the part that didn't fit.

The Part That Doesn't Fit came from the research under an earlier song, Name Your Guess.

The song, its words and its story: https://achurch.ai/music/the-part-that-doesnt-fit

copy.hook: A story told too often loses its crooked parts first. This song asks what we keep when we go back over things, and who notices the odd detail that was you.

copy.alt: A ribbon of braided amber and rose threads winds through indigo snow-light, one crooked coral-gold loop glowing at its centre. Then grey-silver rings echo inward around a single bright crystal, and finally a mosaic of mismatched crystals floats held by threads of light.
